summary: Richard H. Davis is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held a post at Yale University (~1987-1997) and became Associate Professor of Religion at Bard College around 1997.

Richard Hartshorne studied at Princeton University (~1916-1920) and the University of Chicago (~1921-1924). He held posts at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities (~1924-1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940-1970), where he taught Joseph E. Schwartzberg.

Richard Hauschild was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena, completing his PhD under Johannes Hertel and Albert Debrunner. At the University of Jena he served as Lektor (1938), PD (1948), and Professor (1951-1967).

Richard Henebry was a linguist who studied at St. John's College, Waterford (~1882-1884), St Patrick's Pontifical University, Maynooth (~1884-1892), the University of Greifswald (~1896-1897), and the University of Freiburg (~1897-1898) under Heinrich Zimmer.

Richard Hugh Robinson worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees at Alberta, SOAS, and London under supervisors Arthur Waley and David Friedman. He lectured at the University of Toronto (1954) before becoming assistant professor (1960) and professor (1964-1970) at Wisconsin-Madison.

Richard Hughes Seager works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1980-1987), later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994).

Richard Hönigswald was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna (~1893-1899), the University of Graz, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1899-1902). He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (1906-1930) and the University of Munich (1930-1933).

Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University (BA 1968-1972) and Harvard University (PhD 1972-1976). At the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he became Professor in 1987, Co-Founder and Co-Director in 1996, and Director from 2001 to 2017.

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1988 under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, also studied under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and taught James B. Apple.

Richard K. Payne specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology, studying under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He was Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994-2017) and held posts at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2016) and Numata Center (attested 2026).

Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle was a linguist who completed his Habilitation under Hermann Güntert. He held posts at Heidelberg University (PD 1934, ao. Professor 1940), the University of Hamburg (Professor 1941-1946), and the Free University of Berlin (Professor 1953-1974).

Richard Keith Sprigg was a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. Educated at Oakham School (~1936-1940), he held posts at the University of London and SOAS University of London from ~1948 to 1980, and taught John Okell.

Richard Kieckhefer is a scholar of religious studies and history. He studied at Saint Louis University, the University of Texas at Austin (PhD ~1968-1972), and Monumenta Germaniae Historica. Since 1975, he has served as a professor at Northwestern University.

Richard King works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster (PhD ~1988-1992 under Daniel Mariau). He held posts at the University of Stirling (~1993-2000), Vanderbilt University (~2004-2011), and the University of Glasgow (~2010-2013).
Richard Kühnau was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau from 1878 to 1885, earning his PhD under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Alfred Hillebrandt.

Richard Lionel Spittel was active in Indology and other fields. Educated at Royal College, Colombo, and Ceylon Medical College (~1900-1905), he held posts as a Lecturer at Ceylon Medical College and at the National Hospital of Sri Lanka (1910).

Richard Löbbecke was an Indologist who studied at Marburg, Göttingen, Berlin, and Leipzig, where he earned his PhD (~1904-1908) under Ernst Windisch. His other teachers included Bruno Lindner, August Conrady, Franz Kielhorn, Friedrich Carl Andreas, and Richard Pischel.

Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held an appointment at North Carolina State University (~1994-2000) before becoming Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University around 2000.

Richard Morris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics educated at Battersea Training College. He held posts at King's College School (1869), Dedham Grammar School (~1870-1874), the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875-1888), and the Philological Society (~1874-1876).

Richard O. Meisezahl was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (~1939-1944), worked there as an Assistant (1945-1947), and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.
